title: PIM for Active Directory: build the hybrid worker's Azure side (or check an Azure Arc server)
purpose: Builds the Azure side of the PIM for Active Directory hybrid worker -- its own resource group, network, deny-all firewall, NAT gateway egress and Windows VM -- or, for an Azure Arc-enabled on-premises server, checks the machine and builds nothing.
whenToRun: Once per hybrid worker, first step. Azure VM worker: with -PeerVnetId and -DnsServers. On-premises worker: with -ArcMachineResourceId after the server is onboarded to Azure Arc. Deploy-PimHybridWorker.ps1 runs it for you.

runAs.name: Contributor
runAs.scope: the worker's subscription (Azure VM); Reader on the Arc machine (Arc)
runAs.why: creates the resource group, VNet, NSG, NAT gateway and VM; reads the Arc machine

runAs.name: Network Contributor
runAs.scope: every VNet the worker peers with (-PeerVnetId)
runAs.why: the script creates both sides of each peering

runAs.name: SQL Server Contributor
runAs.why: the VNet rule for the worker subnet (Azure VM) or the firewall rules for -SqlAllowedPublicIp (Arc)

changes.object: resource group, VNet + subnet (Microsoft.Sql and Microsoft.Storage service endpoints, DNS = your DCs), NSG with deny-all inbound, NAT gateway + its public IP (Set-PimHybridWorkerEgress.ps1), peerings in both directions, the VM (Windows Server 2022 Azure Edition Core, Trusted Launch, system-assigned identity, NO public IP), a SQL VNet rule
changes.why: the worker's own isolated network and machine; the local admin password is generated, used once and discarded
changes.undo: delete the resource group, the remote peerings and the SQL VNet rule 'pimhybridwrk'

changes.object: a virtual network link 'link-pimhybridwrk-<vnet>' (tagged pim-hybrid-worker) to the worker VNet and each -PrivateDnsLinkVnetId; the standard zone itself only with -CreatePrivateDnsZone when missing; a DNS zone group on the SQL private endpoint only when its A record is missing and the endpoint has none
changes.why: a private-only PIM database must resolve to its private address; the DCs' conditional forwarder is printed, never written
changes.undo: Remove-PimHybridWorker.ps1 (the worker VNet's link); delete other links yourself

changes.object: useRemoteGateways / allowForwardedTraffic on the worker-side peering; allowGatewayTransit on the hub side only when PIM created that peering (otherwise printed for the hub owner)
changes.why: DCs reached through a hub VPN / ExpressRoute gateway
changes.undo: Set-PimHybridWorkerPeering.ps1 cannot turn them off; set them in the portal, or remove the worker

changes.object: one firewall rule per on-premises egress address (pimhybridwrk-arc-<server>-<n>)
changes.why: an on-premises worker reaching a public SQL endpoint; not needed with a private endpoint

parameters.name: SubscriptionId
parameters.help: The worker's subscription (Azure VM) or the Arc machine's.

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: The tenant; the script refuses a subscription in another one.

parameters.name: ArcMachineResourceId
parameters.help: On-premises worker: the Azure Arc machine's resource id. Builds nothing; checks it is connected, Windows and has an identity.

parameters.name: ArcApiVersion
parameters.help: Microsoft.HybridCompute api-version.

parameters.name: SqlAllowedPublicIp
parameters.help: Arc with a public SQL endpoint: the site's egress address(es).

parameters.name: ResourceGroup
parameters.help: Azure VM: the worker's resource group.

parameters.name: Location
parameters.help: Azure VM: the region (your choice).

parameters.name: VmName
parameters.help: Azure VM: VM and computer name, max 15 characters.

parameters.name: VmSize
parameters.help: Azure VM: the size (4 GiB recommended).

parameters.name: VnetName
parameters.help: Azure VM: the worker VNet.

parameters.name: AddressPrefix
parameters.help: Azure VM: VNet range (must not overlap the peered networks).

parameters.name: SubnetPrefix
parameters.help: Azure VM: the worker subnet.

parameters.name: PeerVnetId
parameters.help: Azure VM (required there): the VNet(s) with the domain controllers, optionally the PIM environment's.

parameters.name: DnsServers
parameters.help: Azure VM (required there): the domain controllers' addresses.

parameters.name: SqlServerId
parameters.help: The PIM SQL server's resource id (VNet rule / firewall rules).

parameters.name: Egress
parameters.help: Azure VM: NatGateway, or None when your network routes outbound. Never a public IP on the VM.

parameters.name: Image
parameters.help: Azure VM: the image (Publisher:Offer:Sku:Version).

parameters.name: PrivateSqlDnsZoneId
parameters.help: Private-only PIM database: the EXISTING privatelink.database.windows.net zone (no other zone name is accepted). It is linked to the worker VNet (Azure VM) and to every -PrivateDnsLinkVnetId.

parameters.name: PrivateDnsLinkVnetId
parameters.help: More VNets to link the zone to: the DCs' VNet when the DCs are Azure VMs (Azure DNS answers from the zones linked to the ASKING DNS server's VNet), or the DNS Private Resolver's VNet (Arc / on-premises DCs).

parameters.name: CreatePrivateDnsZone
parameters.help: Create the standard zone privatelink.database.windows.net ONLY when it is missing (with -PrivateDnsZoneResourceGroup or -PrivateSqlDnsZoneId); attaches it to the SQL private endpoint when that endpoint has no DNS zone group yet.

parameters.name: PrivateDnsZoneResourceGroup
parameters.help: Where the standard zone lives (in -SubscriptionId), instead of -PrivateSqlDnsZoneId.

parameters.name: PrivateSql
parameters.help: Print the conditional forwarder the DNS administrator adds (implied by the zone options). PIM never writes AD / on-premises DNS.

parameters.name: DnsForwarderIp
parameters.default: 168.63.129.16 (Azure VM) / the Private Resolver inbound endpoint (Arc)
parameters.help: The address the printed forwarder points at: 168.63.129.16 for DCs that are Azure VMs, an Azure DNS Private Resolver inbound endpoint for DCs on-premises.

parameters.name: UseRemoteGateways
parameters.help: Azure VM: DCs reached through the hub's VPN / ExpressRoute gateway -- the worker-side peering to -GatewayVnetId uses it (Set-PimHybridWorkerPeering.ps1; the hub must have a gateway and allow gateway transit).

parameters.name: GatewayVnetId
parameters.help: Azure VM: the hub VNet with the gateway (one of -PeerVnetId).

parameters.name: AllowForwardedTraffic
parameters.help: Azure VM: the worker-side peering(s) accept traffic the hub forwards (an NVA / firewall in the hub).

readsOnly: what already exists (read-before-write): resource group, NSG, VNet, peerings, VM, SQL rules
network: management.azure.com (ARM REST) and login.microsoftonline.com -- browser sign-in or an Invardia support session; no Azure CLI, no PowerShell module
whatIf: Prints every resource it would create (or, for Arc, the checks and the firewall rules) and changes nothing.
undo: Remove-PimHybridWorker.ps1 deletes everything this script created (it carries the tag pim-hybrid-worker). By hand: Azure VM: delete the worker's resource group, the remote peerings '<remote>-to-pimhybridwrk', the SQL VNet rule 'pimhybridwrk' and the zone link. Arc: delete the pimhybridwrk-arc-* SQL firewall rules.
